source_issues.explanation: The printed equality Zh intersect(ell z0+Lambda)={0} for every ell is literally too strong:0 need not be in a nonzero coset, and for ell=1 a finite wp(z0) implies z0 is not a lattice point. The author immediately gives the stronger GROUP-intersection condition Zh intersect(Zz0+Lambda)={0} at1272 and proves exactly that condition at1411-1426. It implies that each relevant coset contains no NONZERO multiple of h, which is exactly all that1317/1372/1377 use. Certify the counted arithmetic theorem through this explicitly authored sufficient branch; do not certify or silently replace the literal coset equality.

For theta_k(z)=theta(z/k), the multiplier in550 is e^(2 pi i omega/k), not e^(2 pi i omega). Accordingly the degree-zero periodicity footnote554 requires omega in kZ for that representative, not merely Z. The original functional equation478, the converse proof570-571 and the actual normal-form uses1126/1134 all explicitly supply the divided exponent. Record the source typo separately and leave the author formula untouched.

The normalization Lambda=Z+tau Z is an analytic coordinate convenience in the generic elliptic difference calculation. The arithmetic hypotheses g2,g3,h,A,B algebraic refer to the ORIGINAL Weierstrass coordinates of76-110. They must not be imposed after a possibly transcendental period rescaling. To identify the convention precisely: if z=omega1 t, then h becomes h/omega1 and wp_Lambda(omega1 t)=omega1^(-2) wp_(Lambda/omega1)(t); the generic theorem allows arbitrary complex a,alpha,beta and its nonresonance condition is unchanged after dividing every term by omega1. The induced difference-field isomorphism preserves the PV group. Thus one applies the already proved generic result in any analytic coordinate, while performing1414-1426 before that rescaling. This explains the author without-loss-of-generality convention; it does not claim that algebraicity of h or the invariants is preserved by normalization.

The Galois cover in419-420 goes from C/(aLambda-double-prime) to C/Lambda-prime, contrary to the written arrow; this is uniquely fixed by the field inclusion418 and the correct contravariant map405-408. At941 the matrix T-double-prime certainly lies in M_(Lambda-double-prime), as defined from T-prime at916-940. The displayed M_(kLambda) is not justified for the fully general pair of sublattices in846 solely from k=[Lambda-prime:Lambda-double-prime]; the proof needs only the already specified M_(Lambda-double-prime) membership and its cyclic Galois action. The actual two application fields are explicitly given at999-1005 and1057-1065.

The author does not expand the first-order check. Under the allowed standard criterion, a finite determinant image would imply b^m=phi(f)/f for some m>=1 and f in K*. On a period cover containing f, the divisor of phi(f)/f has sum0 on every h-orbit, by finite-support telescoping. In the orbit of0 modulo that period lattice, b^m has a double pole of multiplicity2m and no zero: a zero would give nh=+/-z0 modulo Lambda, forbidden by the authored nonresonance condition, while nontorsion separates the lattice poles. Its orbit sum is therefore -2m, contradiction. Hence the determinant image is infinite and thus G_m. This verifies the standard compressed step from the already printed divisor and hypotheses; do not present these reviewer sentences as missing author prose or as a new separately counted proof.
